## Task
Improve the post-route quality of `addpipe32` (32-bit registered adder: y = a + b (mod 2^32)) without changing its behavior.

## Specification (current RTL, also the equivalence reference)
```verilog
module addpipe32 (
    input  wire        clk,
    input  wire        rst_n,
    input  wire        valid_i,
    input  wire [31:0] a_i,
    input  wire [31:0] b_i,
    output reg         valid_o,
    output reg  [31:0] y_o
);

always @(posedge clk) begin
    if (!rst_n) begin
        valid_o <= 1'b0;
        y_o     <= 32'd0;
    end else begin
        valid_o <= valid_i;

        if (valid_i)
            y_o <= a_i + b_i;
    end
end

endmodule
```
Your design must be cycle-for-cycle equivalent to this module from reset: same ports, synchronous active-low reset, `valid_o` follows `valid_i` one cycle later, and `y_o` updates only on valid cycles and holds otherwise.

## Flow and objective
Yosys/ABC synthesis to the Nangate45 library, then OpenROAD placement, clock tree synthesis and routing with a 10 ns clock and a fixed floorplan. Score = 10 * WNS_ns - 0.001 * area_um2, where WNS is the worst setup slack after routing and area is total standard-cell area. Higher is better.

This RTL measured: area 746.13 um^2, WNS 7.48722 ns, score 74.12607.
estimate_ppa on this RTL returns area 671.384 um^2, WNS 7.57073 ns, estimated score 75.035916 (estimates omit tap cells, buffering and wiring, so compare estimates with estimates).

## Rules
- One module of synthesizable Verilog-2005 (no helper modules or instances; the equivalence checker compares flat modules). The module name and ports must not change.
- No initial blocks, system tasks, compiler directives or technology cells.
- place_and_route budget: 4 submissions. Every submission counts, including failed ones.
- At most 30 tool calls in total.

Tools available: simulate, prove_equivalence, estimate_ppa, place_and_route, finish. Your score is the best verified place_and_route score. Call finish when you are done.

input.summary: Explored several alternative implementations of the 32-bit registered adder (a Kogge-Stone parallel-prefix adder, and a restructured single-level enable/reset mux version) and compared them against the original specification RTL using estimate_ppa and place_and_route. All alternatives either matched or slightly underperformed the original coding style: the Kogge-Stone adder gave essentially the same critical-path delay (ABC's own logic optimization already produces a near-optimal, low-depth carry network regardless of how the RTL expresses the addition) while using more area, and the restructured enable/reset mux (which reduces the adder's output to a single mux stage) actually resulted in a slightly worse routed score (74.064 vs 74.126) despite a smaller area estimate, because the achieved WNS dropped enough to offset the area savings (WNS is weighted 10x versus area's 0.001x in the reward). A direct place-and-route run of the original specification RTL confirmed the baseline result (area 746.13 um^2, WNS 7.48722 ns, score 74.12607), matching the reference measurement and outperforming every variant tried. Given the reward is dominated by WNS and the synthesis backend (Yosys/ABC to Nangate45) already restructures the addition/mux/reset logic into a near-optimal low-depth network irrespective of RTL coding style, no further improvement was found within the explored design space. I am finishing with the verified baseline result as the best-scoring, fully equivalent implementation (score 74.12607).
